milestones.label: Kolmogorov's empirical distribution (goodness-of-fit) test
milestones.work: Kolmogoroff, A., Sulla determinazione empirica di una legge di distribuzione, 1933 (zbMATH 2546673)
milestones.description: Kolmogorov used the distribution-function framework of probability to build a statistical test that compares an empirical distribution with a hypothesised one.

evidence.claim: zbMATH records a 1933 paper by Kolmogorov titled 'Sulla determinazione empirica di una legge di distribuzione'
The Kolmogorov-Smirnov test statistic and its null distribution were first published by Kolmogorov in 1933

milestones.note: Weak fit to the idea. The 1933 paper is a statistical application of probability via distribution functions, and I did not verify that it uses the measure-theoretic framework of the Grundbegriffe (same year). Its year is not later than the listed first_statement (1933), so it qualifies only by the same-year rule. Reviewer should decide whether this counts as measure theory meeting probability.

zbMATH search: 'Sulla determinazione empirica' (two 1933 records, one per entry)
Wikipedia raw wikitext: Borel and Kolmogorov context not used because Borel 1909 falls before the listed first_statement 1933

milestones.label: Perfectoid spaces used to construct Galois representations on torsion cohomology
milestones.work: Scholze, P., On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties, arXiv:1306.2070 (submitted 9 June 2013); Ann. of Math. (2) 182 (2015), 945-1066
milestones.description: Scholze used the perfectoid space of level-p structures and its Hodge-Tate period map to build Galois representations attached to torsion classes in the cohomology of GL_n locally symmetric varieties.

evidence.claim: arXiv 1306.2070 by Peter Scholze, 'On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties', submitted 9 June 2013
Annals of Mathematics 182 (2015), 945-1066; the review says the infinite level cover is a perfectoid space with a Hodge-Tate period map, used to realise torsion classes

milestones.note: Year is the arXiv submission year; the journal version is 2015. Perfectoid spaces were introduced in Scholze's 2012 IHES paper (the first_statement). I did not check whether that 2012 paper already contains an earlier application, nor find a history page (Wikipedia's perfectoid article has none). The application is substantive, but 'first' is not fully established.

milestones.label: Topological modular functor shown universal for quantum computation
milestones.work: Freedman, M. H., Larsen, M., Wang, Z., A modular functor which is universal for quantum computation, arXiv:quant-ph/0001108 (submitted 29 January 2000); Comm. Math. Phys. 227 (2002), DOI 10.1007/s002200200645
milestones.description: The authors showed that the topological modular functor of Chern-Simons theory can approximate any quantum circuit computation, applying anyonic topology to the target problem of universal quantum computation.

evidence.claim: arXiv quant-ph/0001108 'A modular functor which is universal for quantum computation' was submitted 29 January 2000
Published in Communications in Mathematical Physics 227 (2002), 605-622, with the title 'A Modular Functor Which is Universal for Quantum Computation'
In 2000 Freedman, Kitaev, Larsen and Wang proved that a topological quantum computer can perform any computation a conventional quantum computer can; Kitaev's 1997 proposal is the first_statement

milestones.note: Companion paper Freedman, Kitaev, Wang, 'Simulation of topological field theories by quantum computers', arXiv quant-ph/0001071 (also 2000; Crossref DOI 10.1007/s002200200635) is a parallel application. I chose the modular-functor paper as the one that states universality. Wikipedia's 2000 date is consistent with the arXiv record.
